11. Operational Reporting and Metrics

Meridian Capital maintains a consolidated, monthly operational reporting suite to evidence the performance, integrity, and client impact of refund and compensation activities across all business lines. The Client Experience Analytics (CEA) function curates this suite using system-of-record extracts from the Refund Management Platform (RMP), Constellation CRM, and the Treasury Payment Gateway (TPG), reconciled to the Financial Subledger (FSL). As of 2026-06-30 23:59 UTC (RMP batch RUNID: RMP-B-2026-06-30-2215; TPG settlement cycle TPG-S-2026-06-30-3), the core key performance indicators (KPIs) remained within tolerance, with noted areas of attention recorded for action by the Client Experience Operations (CXO) leadership and Technology Delivery – Client Payments (TD‑CP).

The KPI framework covers timeliness, quality, and client experience outcomes. Refund Cycle Time measures elapsed business days from case submission to disbursement confirmation, tracked at median, 90th, and 95th percentiles. First-Contact Refund Resolution Rate (FCRR) measures the proportion of eligible claims resolved at initial contact without subsequent touchpoints. Service-Level Attainment reflects the share of cases decided within product-specific service standards. Aging Distribution segments the active backlog into 0–5, 6–10, and >10 business day buckets. Reopen Rate quantifies the percentage of closed cases subsequently reopened due to additional client information or quality review. Erroneous Denial Rate (EDR) measures the percentage of decisions reversed on appeal or quality sampling due to adjudication error. Goodwill Gesture Frequency and Average Ex-Gratia Amount provide calibrated visibility into discretionary compensation deployed to remedy process inconvenience where monetary loss is not present.

For Q2 FY2026, the average refund cycle time was 3.2 business days (P90: 5.3; P95: 6.9), with FCRR at 71.4% on digitally originated cases and 64.8% on assisted channels. SLA attainment across portfolios was 98.4%, with isolated departures linked to a partner bank settlement constraint on 2026-05-18 (incident INC-CP-2026-05-18-0192) and a subsequent clearing delay on 2026-06-07 (problem PRB-RFD-2026-06-07-0004). Both items were reviewed by Treasury Operations (TRO) and Partner Management (PMO), and corrective action tracking was initiated under CAPA-RFD-2026-06-21-0001, entered at 2026-06-21 14:08 UTC, to reinforce calendarized cutoffs and proactive exception messaging to clients. The Aging Distribution as of period end showed 82.1% of open claims in 0–5 business days, 14.9% in 6–10, and 3.0% >10, with the long-tail predominantly attributable to incomplete documentation requiring client follow-up (reference cases REF-2026-06-14-00312; REF-2026-06-22-00147) and multi-institution reconciliations.

Quality and correctness indicators demonstrated continued improvement. The EDR trended down to 0.7% (rolling three-month basis), below the KRI-RFD-006 threshold of 1.2%, supported by targeted adjudicator coaching administered by the Quality Assurance Office (QAO) following the monthly calibration session held 2026-06-19 09:30–11:00 UTC (session note QA-SN-2026-06-19-REF). The Reopen Rate measured 4.6%, with root-cause tags dominated by “late evidence submission” and “misclassification of product type,” both addressed in CXO refresher modules. Goodwill gestures were applied at a rate of 7.3 per 1,000 contacts, with an average ex-gratia amount of 28.45 USD where service inconvenience was evidenced without direct monetary detriment; Governance Review (GVN-2026-06-27-02) affirmed alignment to the Compensation Calibration Guide v4.1.

Channel-level performance remained stable. Digital self-service submissions, which constituted 56.2% of total intake in June, maintained a lower average cycle time (2.6 business days) relative to assisted channels (3.9 business days), attributable to higher initial data completeness. Assisted volumes exhibited greater variance due to cases that originated via phone after-hours routing and required subsequent verification. The CXO Scheduling and Workforce team reconciled these dynamics in the mid-month capacity review (WFM-2026-06-17-M1), reallocating senior adjudicators to the evening queue to compress the 90th percentile turnaround by 0.3 days without compromising quality controls or client communication cadence.

The periodic Management Information (MI) pack includes trend visualizations for five consecutive quarters, enabling the Refund Governance Forum to evaluate structural changes, seasonal effects, and the impact of process enhancements. For example, the introduction of guided evidence prompts in Constellation CRM on 2026-04-29 (change RFC-CRM-2026-04-29-088) correlates with a 12% reduction in late-evidence-related reopens over May–June. Similarly, the refined rejection rationale taxonomy, deployed 2026-05-09 (RFC-RMP-2026-05-09-064), improved QAO sampling efficiency by enabling stratified selections across denial categories R1–R4, thereby enhancing insight into training needs and rule clarity.

The Control and Assurance overlay integrates both leading and lagging indicators. Key Control Indicators (KCIs) monitored by first line include completeness of case chronology notes, linkage to disbursement voucher IDs, and confirmation timestamps from TPG. Monthly testing by the Finance Controls and Assurance (FCA) team validates the reconciliation between RMP disbursement records and FSL postings, with June variances well within the immaterial threshold set by the Finance Policy Council (FPC). Where tickets require cross-functional intervention, the Service Desk assigns enterprise references that remain visible across platforms; representative examples include SVC-REF-2026-06-03-1027 (batch confirmation lag), SVC-REF-2026-06-15-1184 (duplicate client submission detection), and SVC-REF-2026-06-28-1231 (clarification of merchant dispute versus fee reversal).

To reinforce transparency, each reporting cycle is accompanied by a management attestation signed by the Process Owner (PO-CXO-RFD) and co-signed by FCA confirming the completeness and accuracy of MI inputs. The attestation for 2026-06 (ATT-REF-2026-06) was executed at 2026-07-01 10:22 UTC, with no reservations noted. Any metrics breaching pre-defined thresholds trigger entries to the Risk Management Office (RMO) watchlist and are escalated to the Client Committee on Service Outcomes at the next sitting, ensuring sustained focus on client restitution, timeliness, and fairness across refund and compensation activities.

12. Governance, Assurance, and Record Retention

This policy is governed within Meridian Capital’s enterprise policy framework and is overseen by the Policy Governance Office (PGO) in coordination with the Client Experience Operations (CXO) leadership. Version v2.3 was approved by the Policy Review Board (PRB) on 2026-07-01 under minute reference PRB-2026-06-29-07, following formal consultation with the Compliance Oversight Unit (COU), Finance Controls and Assurance (FCA), and Technology Delivery – Client Payments (TD‑CP). The designated Policy Owner is the Head of Client Experience Operations (PO-CXO-RFD), with the Document Steward assigned to PGO (ST-POL-REF). The next scheduled review date is 2027-06-30, or earlier upon material regulatory or operational change. Controlled copies are maintained within the enterprise Policy Hub with document identifier POL-REF-2.3 and distribution list DL-POL-REF-ENT.

Governance operates through a layered model integrating decision rights, independent challenge, and evidentiary oversight. The Refund Governance Forum convenes monthly, chaired by CXO, with standing participation from COU, FCA, RMO, TD‑CP, Treasury Operations (TRO), and Data Management (DMT). The Forum’s remit includes review of the operational MI pack, client outcome themes, quality trends, and remediation status against open actions logged within the Corrective and Preventive Action register (CAPA-RFD). All decisions and action allocations are recorded with ticket-level traceability; for example, action A‑RFD‑2026‑06‑27‑03 was raised to refine the case note template to better surface compensation rationale, with TD‑CP delivery tracked under RFC-RMP-2026-07-143 and UAT evidence filed as QTP‑REF‑2026‑07‑143E (UAT window 2026-07-12 to 2026-07-16).

Independent assurance is provided through the Three Lines model. First line executes the process and performs control self-assessments, including monthly KCI testing on case chronology completeness and reconciliation sign-offs (CSA-REF-2026-06 filed 2026-06-28). Second line (COU) conducts thematic monitoring in line with the Compliance Monitoring Plan CMP‑2026‑REF‑02; a Q3 2026 review will reperform a stratified sample of 500 closed cases across products to assess adherence to timeliness standards and fairness criteria. Third line (Internal Audit) has scheduled a targeted audit for 2026-08 under engagement IA‑2026‑17, with a scope encompassing case lifecycle controls, compensation decision frameworks, and financial integrity of disbursements. All prior audit findings relevant to refunds and compensation have been addressed; notably, IA‑2025‑09‑F2 (case documentation specificity) was closed on 2026-03-12 per closure memo IA‑2025‑09‑CLOSE‑03 following deployment of enhanced note prompts.

Record retention and auditability are central to ensuring transparent, reconstructible outcomes. Case records, including submission artifacts, adjudication notes, decision communications, and disbursement confirmations, are retained for seven years from case closure per Retention Schedule RS‑FIN‑018 and Data Privacy Standard DPS‑GEN‑05. Each case is anchored by a unique case identifier (e.g., REF‑YYYY‑MM‑DD‑NNNNN) and cross-referenced to the corresponding disbursement voucher ID and FSL journal entries, with time-stamped milestones in UTC. Interaction logs from Constellation CRM, including inbound calls, secure messages, and notifications, form part of the permanent audit trail, enabling end-to-end reconstruction. The FCA monthly reconciliation pack (REC‑RFD‑MM‑YYYY) links total approved compensation to posted disbursements and ledger balances; the June 2026 pack (REC‑RFD‑06‑2026) reconciled to within the established tolerance with no unresolved breaks at close (2026‑06‑30 22:40 UTC).

Change governance ensures stability and measured improvement. Any modification to refund rules, decision matrices, or compensation calibration thresholds is introduced via the formal Request for Change (RFC) process and assessed by the Change Advisory Board – Payments (CAB‑PAY). For instance, RFC‑TPG‑2026‑07‑143 (adjustment to disbursement window labelling for client communications) received CAB approval on 2026‑07‑05 and completed non-disruptive implementation on 2026‑07‑13 02:15 UTC, with post‑implementation validation recorded in CHG‑PIR‑2026‑07‑143. Business owners file pre‑implementation impact assessments (BUS‑IA‑REF‑####) and secure sign-offs attesting that client outcome quality is preserved or enhanced. All evidence is retained in the Enterprise Change Repository (ECR) with cross-references to CAPA or governance actions where applicable.

Training and competency underpin consistent, fair decisions. All adjudicators, case handlers, and team leads complete onboarding curriculum LMS‑REF‑101 (Policy and Standards) and LMS‑REF‑102 (Decisioning and Documentation), followed by annual refresher LMS‑REF‑201, with assessments tracked in the Learning Management System. As of 2026‑06‑30, completion for in-scope colleagues was 99.2% (LMS‑RPT‑2026‑06‑EOM), with outstanding items already scheduled for completion in early July (tickets HR‑EDU‑2026‑07‑0041 to ‑0043). Periodic calibration sessions led by QAO ensure alignment on case categorization and compensation rationales, with calibration artifacts preserved under QA‑CAL‑YYYY‑MM identifiers. Supervisory reviews are conducted per the Quality Review Framework, and coaching notes are recorded in Constellation CRM against the reviewer record to support continuity and accountability.

Operational resilience is validated through periodic exercises. The most recent scenario test (SIM‑2026‑04‑18‑BCP‑RFD) validated continuity of refund case intake and adjudication under constrained system availability, confirming that client communications remained timely and accurate and that disbursement confirmations were properly queued for transmission upon restoration. Findings were closed under BCP‑FND‑2026‑04‑18‑01 through ‑03 by 2026‑05‑10, with evidence retained by the Business Continuity Office. Dependencies on partner institutions are inventoried and reviewed quarterly, with Partner Management maintaining a current view of settlement windows and known constraints to inform SLA design and client messaging.

Communications and attestations complete the governance cycle. Following each monthly Refund Governance Forum, a summary note is circulated to the Client Committee on Service Outcomes and the Executive Risk Committee, with key messages, actions, and metric highlights (GOV‑MIN‑RFD‑2026‑06 issued 2026‑06‑28 16:45 UTC). Policy attestations are collected annually (ATT‑REF‑YYYY) via the enterprise attestation platform, confirming awareness and adherence by all in-scope teams. Queries and requests for clarification are directed to the Policy Owner mailbox (PO‑CXO‑RFD@meridiancapital.example) and logged under POL‑QRY‑YYYY‑NNNN identifiers in the policy query register for traceability and thematic analysis. Collectively, these governance, assurance, and record-keeping measures ensure that refund and compensation activities remain consistent, transparent, and aligned to Meridian Capital’s commitment to fair client outcomes and robust financial integrity.
